Mortgage Affordability Calculator (UAE)

See how much you can borrow and what you can afford to buy

Your budget depends on two limits: what your income can repay, and how much cash you have for the down payment and fees. This calculator checks both and tells you which one holds you back.

Your savings set the limit

Your income could support a loan of about AED 2,223,781, but at 80% LTV your savings cannot cover the rest of a pricier home and its costs. More savings would raise your budget.

This is an estimate, not a lending decision. Limits reflect commonly reported rules reviewed in November 2026, and banks may apply stricter ones.

How It Works

Maximum payment = income × debt limit − existing debts
Cash needed = price × (1 + costs) − loan

The calculator finds the highest price at which your loan fits both your maximum payment and the LTV limit, and your savings cover the rest.

Example: AED 30,000 monthly income, AED 2,000 in existing debt payments, a 5% rate over 25 years and AED 500,000 in savings. Your income supports borrowing up to about AED 2,223,781, but your savings cap the property price at about AED 1,851,852, with a loan of AED 1,481,481 and a monthly payment of AED 8,661.

How to Use This Calculator

  1. Enter your monthly income. Banks may not count all allowances or variable pay
  2. Add your existing debt payments, including loans and credit cards
  3. Set the debt limit. The regulatory maximum is 50%, but try 40% to 45% for a more cautious estimate
  4. Enter the rate, term and savings available for the purchase
  5. Set the buying costs and LTV. About 7% in costs is typical for a resale bought with an agent and a mortgage

Frequently Asked Questions

How much mortgage can I get on my salary in the UAE?
It depends on your income, debts, rate and term. The Central Bank's debt burden limit means total monthly debt payments generally cannot exceed 50% of your income, and many banks apply a stricter internal limit. Enter your figures above to see an estimate.
What is the debt burden ratio (DBR)?
It is your total monthly debt payments as a share of your monthly income, including the new mortgage. Credit cards count too, and banks often include a percentage of your card limit even if you pay it in full, so closing unused cards can raise what you can borrow.
How much down payment do I need in the UAE?
For a first home up to AED 5 million, buyers commonly need at least 20% as an expat or 15% as a UAE national. Requirements are usually higher above AED 5 million, on second homes and on off-plan property, and sources differ on the exact figures. Ask your bank what applies to you.
What is the longest mortgage term in the UAE?
Generally 25 years, and the loan usually needs to be repaid by about age 65 for salaried borrowers or 70 for the self-employed. Older buyers may therefore have a shorter term and a smaller loan.
Will a bank lend me this much?
Not necessarily. This is an estimate of the regulatory limits, not an offer. Banks also look at your credit score, employer, length of service, minimum salary and the property's valuation.
